# Multi-state spliceosome structures predict pathogenic variants in small nuclear RNA genes and separate dominant from recessive disease mechanisms

*Draft v0.1, 7 October 2026. All numbers are generated by the scripts named in brackets; label set v5 unless stated.*

## Abstract

**Background.** Variants in spliceosomal small nuclear RNA (snRNA) genes are among the most frequent causes of
neurodevelopmental disorders (ReNU syndrome, RNU4-2; RNU2-2; RNU5B-1) and also cause recessive multisystem disorders
(RNU4ATAC, RNU12, RNU6ATAC) and retinitis pigmentosa (RNU4-2, RNU6 genes). Current guidance states that no in silico
tool captures features relevant to snRNA variant deleteriousness and that genome-wide predictors perform poorly.

**Methods.** We built snRNA-VEP, which represents each snRNA nucleotide by its protein and RNA contacts across 11
cryo-EM structures spanning the splicing cycle (tri-snRNP to post-catalytic P complex, plus minor-spliceosome states),
projects paralogs and minor-spliceosome analogs onto shared coordinates, and propagates contact information over a
multi-state 3D contact graph. Evidence is combined per disease mechanism, with the scorer for each mechanism chosen by
nested leave-one-gene-out cross-validation. We curated 266 pathogenic variants in 10 genes from 14 sources and used
mechanism-aware controls, including homozygous variants from 490,000 UK Biobank genomes for recessive genes.

**Results.** On genes held out entirely from training, snRNA-VEP reached a mean AUROC of 0.80 for dominant variants
(CADD 0.66, phyloP 0.60; paired ΔAUROC vs CADD +0.19, 95% CI 0.10–0.28, p<0.001). Without any RNU4-2 labels it
correlated with saturation-genome-editing damage in RNU4-2 (ρ=0.40; CADD 0.07; phyloP 0.00). Trained only on knowledge
public before May 2025, it predicted variants that became pathogenic in ClinVar afterwards (dominant mean AUROC 0.76;
ΔAUROC vs CADD +0.17, p=0.009). Dominant pathogenic variants were enriched at contacts with the activation and catalytic
machinery (PRPF8, SART1, RBM42, SNRNP200/Brr2, SNRNP27), whereas recessive variants were enriched at snRNP-assembly
contacts (SNU13 k-turn), and were better captured by conservation. A sequence language model (RNA-FM) failed on
dominant variants (AUROC 0.47). Recessive prediction from position remained limited (AUROC 0.63–0.69 for all methods)
once healthy homozygous carriers were used as controls.

**Conclusions.** Multi-state structural context identifies dominant snRNA disease variants that sequence conservation and
genome-wide predictors miss, and reveals distinct structural signatures of dominant and recessive snRNA disease.
Precomputed scores for 13,280 variants in 17 spliceosomal snRNA genes are provided.

## Introduction (outline)
1. snRNA genes as a major, recently discovered cause of NDD: RNU4-2 (ReNU; ~0.4% of NDD), RNU2-2, RNU5B-1; recessive
   RNU4ATAC, RNU12, RNU6ATAC, biallelic RNU4-2/RNU2-2; RP in RNU4-2/RNU6. High mutability (~50× de novo rate).
2. Interpretation bottleneck: tiny genes, many VUS, CADD/phyloP uninformative (CADD AUC 0.65 vs SGE 0.95 in RNU4-2);
   2026 guidance: no tool captures snRNA-relevant features; snRNA structure changes across the splicing cycle and "may
   not be captured by the analysis of a single structure".
3. Idea: the spliceosome is one of the best-characterised RNP machines structurally; a nucleotide's importance is defined
   by what it touches, in which state. Dominant (altered-function) and recessive (loss-of-function) mechanisms should
   leave different structural signatures.
4. Contributions: (i) multi-state structural VEP with paralog/analog transfer; (ii) mechanism-aware evaluation with
   held-out genes, SGE zero-shot, prospective ClinVar and time splits; (iii) structural mechanism of dominant vs recessive
   snRNA disease; (iv) curated label set with UK Biobank homozygote controls and a precomputed score resource.

## Results

### 1. A curated, mechanism-aware benchmark (05b, 05e, 05f–05h)
266 distinct pathogenic variants (RNU2-2 125, RNU4-2 63, RNU4ATAC 51, RNU6ATAC 9, RNU5B-1 7, RNU12 7, RNU6-1/2/8/9 4)
from 14 sources (9 cohort papers, ClinVar 2026-10, 4 papers from 2026), each reference-checked on GRCh38. Controls are
mechanism-specific: gnomAD v4.1 carriers for dominant-only genes; UK Biobank/All of Us variants for RNU4-2
(gnomAD-independent); for recessive genes only homozygous carriers (gnomAD v4.1 and UK Biobank WGS, ~490k genomes) and
ClinVar B/LB. UK Biobank showed no homozygotes in RNU2-2 n.1–69 or RNU12 n.1–41, and 16 labelled recessive pathogenic
variants carried homozygously by ≥1 adult (likely hypomorphic alleles or label errors; removed in sensitivity set v5c).
Curation caught a systematic numbering offset: literature numbers RNU4ATAC on NR_023343.1, 1 nt upstream of the GENCODE
model (validated on seven classic variants against ClinVar).

### 2. Structural contact profiles across the splicing cycle (04c, 08)
11 human cryo-EM structures (3JCR, 6QW6 tri-snRNP; 6QX9 pre-B; 5O9Z B; 6FF7 Bact; 5Z56 Bact-mature; 5XJC C*; 6QDV P;
6Y5Q U2 snRNP; 8Y6O minor pre-B; 7DVQ minor Bact). snRNA chains are matched by sequence; positions are projected to
family coordinates (U1/U2/U4/U5/U6; U4atac→U4, U6atac→U6, U12→U2, U11→U1). 701 family positions; RNA–RNA contacts
in any state define a multi-state contact graph.

### 3. Structure identifies dominant variants on held-out genes (11, 16; Fig. 1)
Dominant mechanism, mean AUROC over 4 held-out genes: snRNA-VEP 0.804 (v2 chosen by nested selection in 4/4 genes) vs
contacts+phyloP 0.700, contacts 0.688, CADD 0.659, phyloP 0.600. Rank-pooled paired ΔAUROC vs CADD +0.192 [0.096,
0.283], vs phyloP +0.181 [0.100, 0.267], vs contacts alone +0.100 [0.048, 0.154] (all p≤0.001). Robust to label sets:
v2 0.807 (v4), 0.826 (v4s, compiled variants ≥2 publications), 0.810 (v5c). The largest model coefficient is the
graph-smoothed contact fraction (3D neighbourhood across states).

### 4. Zero-shot agreement with saturation genome editing (12; Fig. 2)
Without RNU4-2 labels (and without any U4-family labels), snRNA-VEP correlated with SGE function scores (ρ=0.40,
485 variants); graph-smoothed contacts alone 0.44, raw contacts 0.35, CADD 0.07, phyloP −0.004.

### 5. Prospective and temporal validation (17, 12)
Trained only on knowledge public before ClinVar 2025-05-04 and only on other genes, snRNA-VEP ranked the 41 variants
classified P/LP afterwards: dominant RNU2-2 0.797, RNU4-2 0.716 (CADD 0.458/0.522; phyloP 0.670/0.382); pooled ΔAUROC
vs CADD +0.173 [0.039, 0.304], p=0.009. Trained on RNU4-2 alone (first gene described), it ranked later-discovered
RNU2-2 dominant variants at 0.719 and RNU6 RP variants at 0.928.

### 6. Dominant and recessive disease leave different structural signatures (18a, 18b; Fig. 3)
Position-level Mantel–Haenszel odds ratios (strata = genes): dominant variants are enriched at contacts with PRPF8
(OR 6.4, FDR 5×10⁻⁴), SART1 (5.8), RBM42 (12.0), SNRNP200/Brr2 (4.4), SNRNP27 (4.9), SF3B1 (13.6) and PPIL2, all
FDR<0.01 — the B-complex activation and catalytic-core machinery; the Sm ring is not enriched (OR 0.8). The RBM42
signal independently recovers the RBM42-interacting region reported for severe ReNU. Recessive variants are enriched at
SNU13 (k-turn) contacts (OR 4.4, FDR 0.036), with SF3A (5.5) and Sm-ring (1.7) trends — snRNP assembly. B-complex
contact separates dominant pathogenic variants best for RNU4-2 (AUROC 0.64) and RNU6 (0.84).

### 7. What does not work, and the limits of recessive prediction (13, 11)
An RNA language model (RNA-FM; masked marginals) captured conservation-like signal (recessive 0.72) but failed on
dominant variants (0.47; inverted for RNU6 at 0.09) and on SGE (ρ≤0.15). Adding RNA-FM and folding features (v3) did
not improve the dominant model (0.814 vs 0.807). With homozygous-carrier controls, recessive variants were hard for all
methods (contacts+phyloP 0.690, phyloP 0.637, CADD 0.627, snRNA-VEP-nested 0.655): rare variants tolerated in the
homozygous state sit in the same 3′ regions as recessive pathogenic variants, implying that recessive pathogenicity
depends on allele severity/hypomorphism rather than position alone.

### 8. Clinical use and resource (14, 19)
Held-out scores reach BP4_supporting (v2<0.24; LR− 0.30) but not PP3 with current label numbers. Precomputed scores:
13,280 variants in 17 genes (results/snrnavep_scores.tsv.gz).

## Discussion (outline)
- Structure, not conservation, marks dominant snRNA disease: snRNAs are uniformly conserved, so conservation cannot rank
  positions within them, but contacts made only in particular states can.
- Mechanistic model: dominant variants perturb activation/catalytic contacts (PRPF8, Brr2, SART1, RBM42) and act through
  altered function; recessive variants weaken snRNP biogenesis (SNU13, Sm) and act through reduced dosage → consistent
  with SGE (dominant depleted, recessive hypomorphic) and with transcriptomic 5′SS phenotypes.
- Implications for ACMG: supports mechanism-specific PP3 evidence and the 2026 guidance call for snRNA-specific tools;
  paralog/analog transfer is formalised by family coordinates.
- Limitations: few positives for RNU5B-1/RNU6; recessive limits; literature-compiled labels (sensitivity analyses);
  GENCODE v27 RNU4-2 141-nt model; structures are of wild-type complexes; no PP3 calibration yet.
- Future: SGE of RNU2-2/RNU5B-1 as prospective tests; RBM42-containing and additional state structures; calibration.

## Methods (outline; details in scripts)
Data: GENCODE v27 (GRCh38), gnomAD v4.1 genomes, UK Biobank WGS AFB (person-exported; QC allele number ≥50% of gene
median), ClinVar 2025-05-04 and 2026-10-04, CADD v1.7, phyloP447 (UCSC), SGE (De Jonghe et al. 2026), RefSeq transcripts.
Features: within-gene percentile ranks (unsupervised, over all possible variants) of protein-contact fraction across
states, maximum protein contacts, snRNA–snRNA contact fraction, graph-smoothed contact fraction (row-normalised adjacency
of RNA–RNA contacts weighted by number of states, plus backbone and self loops), phyloP447.
Model: L2 logistic regression (C=0.3, balanced) on features × mechanism context; nested leave-one-unit-out selection
among {v2, contacts+phyloP, contacts, phyloP}. Units: RNU4-2, RNU2-2, RNU5B-1, RNU6 genes (one unit), RNU4ATAC, RNU12;
a unit is evaluated if it has ≥3 pathogenic and ≥3 controls (RNU6ATAC training-only).
Statistics: AUROC with bootstrap CIs; paired bootstrap of rank-pooled ΔAUROC (within-unit percentile ranks, 2,000
replicates); Mantel–Haenszel ORs with BH-FDR. Negative/abandoned models (graph neural network v0, SGC v1, v3) reported.
